transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having these eating episodes, and afterward I just feel really gross and disappointed in myself. Like I should’ve had more control, you know? I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it’s been bothering me enough that I’ll end up writing pretty awful things about myself in my journal afterward.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after these eating episodes?
Um… I don’t think so. I mean, not like deliberately making myself throw up, no. I’ve felt really uncomfortable afterward, but I haven’t been doing that. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever exercise excessively after these eating episodes to try to burn off the calories?

I don’t think so… not in a planned way to, like, cancel it out. I mean, my job is pretty physical sometimes, so I’m on my feet a lot, but I wouldn’t say I go exercise after on purpose to burn it off. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
How often do these eating episodes happen?

Um… it’s not every day or anything. But for the past few months, there’s usually been at least one night a week where after work I’ll buy too much food and then eat it all in one stretch. I don’t think I can remember a recent month where it stopped for more than, like, a week or so.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics after these eating episodes?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I know what laxatives are, but I don’t take them after eating or anything like that. Diuretics… I’m not totally sure what all counts, but I’m not doing something on purpose afterward to, um, get rid of it. Is that okay to say?
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating, even if it's not a regular behavior?
No… I mean, I’ve felt really uncomfortable or guilty after, but I haven’t made myself throw up. I know that’s something people ask about, but that’s not something I do.
Do you ever fast or severely restrict your food intake after one of these eating episodes?

I don’t think I really fast, no. Like, I might tell myself I’ll “be better” the next day or eat lighter, but I don’t go a whole day without eating on purpose or anything extreme. At least… I don’t think so. Is that what you mean?
How many months have you been experiencing these eating episodes at a frequency of at least once a week?

Um… I guess it’s been several months. I don’t have an exact number, sorry. But usually there’s at least one night a week where after work I end up buying too much food and eating it all in one stretch. I can’t really think of a recent month where it stopped for more than maybe a week or so. Does that answer it okay?
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but once I start, it’s like I just keep reaching for the next thing without really deciding to. I’ll even be thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” and then I still don’t stop until the food is gone or I feel really uncomfortable. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you usually feel guilty or self-critical after these eating episodes?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try not to make a huge thing out of it, but that’s kind of why I came in. Afterward I just feel really gross and disappointed in myself, like I should’ve had more control.

Sometimes I’ll write in my journal and it gets… pretty mean, honestly. Like awful things about myself that I wouldn’t say to someone else. I know that probably isn’t helpful. But yes, guilty and self-critical is definitely there.
Do you ever use any methods to try to prevent weight gain after these eating episodes?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, not in any organized way. I’ll sometimes tell myself I should “make up for it” or be more careful the next day, but I don’t really have, like, a specific method I use after. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the best way to describe it. I don’t want to overstate it, but once I start, it feels kind of automatic—like I just keep reaching for the next thing.

Even if I’m thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” I don’t actually stop. Usually it’s not until the food is gone or I feel too uncomfortable. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like you're eating much more rapidly than usual during these episodes?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but during those times I’m definitely eating faster than I normally would.

Sometimes I’m just standing at the counter, or sitting on my bed with my sketchbook still open, and I’m kind of just… getting it down. I’m not really tasting it much. It’s like I’m trying to finish before I have time to think about it, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Um… I don’t think I’ve noticed anything really significant. My weight kind of goes up and down a little, I guess, but I haven’t been tracking it closely.

I mean, my clothes feel mostly the same, so… I don’t think there’s been a big change? Is that the kind of thing you mean?
On average, how many times a week do you have one of these eating episodes where you feel like you're unable to stop eating?

Um… probably once a week, most weeks. It’s not like every night or anything, but for the past few months there’s usually been at least one night where after work I buy way too much food and then eat it all in one stretch.

I’m trying to think of a recent month where it really stopped, and… I don’t think it’s gone more than maybe a week or so without happening. Does that sound like the kind of frequency you’re asking for?
Have you experienced any periods of significant weight gain followed by significant weight loss over the past few months?

I don’t think so, no. Not anything I’d call significant, at least.

My weight kind of fluctuates a little, but I haven’t had, like, a big gain and then a big drop that I’ve noticed. I’m not weighing myself all the time, though, so I guess I could be missing small changes… but nothing obvious to me.
Do you feel like you have no control over what or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying it that way, because it sounds like I’m just not trying, but once I start, it kind of feels automatic.

Like I’ll be thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” but I just keep reaching for the next thing anyway. And then I usually don’t really stop until the food is gone, or I feel too uncomfortable to keep going. Is that what you mean by no control?
During these episodes, do you feel like you're eating an amount of food that's definitely more than most people would eat under similar circumstances?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s definitely more than what I think most people would eat for just dinner.

Like after my cleaning shift, I’ll tell myself I’m just grabbing something quick from the convenience store, and then I end up with ramen, a few rice balls, fried chicken, and sweets… and I’ll eat all of it in my room within maybe an hour or two. So, yeah, probably more than most people would have in that situation.
Do you ever do anything to try to counteract the calories you consumed during one of these eating episodes?

Um… not really, I don’t think so.

Like, I might feel guilty and tell myself I should “do better” the next day, but I don’t have a specific thing I do to make up for it. I’m sorry, is that what you mean?
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the best way to describe it, even though I don’t like admitting that.

It’s like once I start, I keep reaching for the next thing almost without deciding to. I’ll be telling myself, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” but I don’t actually stop. Usually it’s only when the food is gone, or I feel too uncomfortable to keep eating.

Does that make sense?
